adjudication_findings.claim: Read-all witnesses must precede minimum-complexity lower bounds.
adjudication_findings.reason: Needed exactly for conclusions of the form G<R(F): with sInf of the empty set equal 0 that conclusion needs nonemptiness. Not needed to use the hypothesis L<R(P), which already excludes L from the set.

presentation.body: For a possibly partial Boolean function $f$, $R(f)$ is the least $q$ for which a probability distribution on deterministic decision trees of depth at most $q$ satisfies $\Pr[T(x)=f(x)]\ge 2/3$ for every $x\in\operatorname{dom}f$. The query cap holds on every branch and for every coin outcome.
presentation.body_plain: For a possibly partial Boolean function f, R(f) is the least q for which a probability distribution on deterministic decision trees of depth at most q satisfies Pr[T(x) = f(x)] ≥ 2/3 for every x ∈ dom f. The query cap holds on every branch and for every coin outcome.
presentation.title: Randomized query complexity $R(f)$

semantic_probes.authored_answer: If the algorithm may depend on the input, it can pick the correct constant answer and spend zero queries. One algorithm chosen in advance cannot compute the one-bit identity with zero queries.

inspection.type:
(∀ (x : QuarticQuery.BitInput (Fin 1)) (b : Bool),
    QuarticQuery.SemanticReview.oneBitIdentity x = Option.some b → ∃ A, A.depth ≤ 0 ∧ 2 / 3 ≤ A.success x b) ∧
  ¬QuarticQuery.RLe QuarticQuery.SemanticReview.oneBitIdentity 0

semantic_probes.question: Could a different zero-query program be chosen after seeing each input?

semantic_probes.authored_answer: On the all-false input the example algorithm for two-bit OR succeeds with probability exactly two thirds. Requiring strictly greater success rules out that algorithm.

inspection.type:
¬∀ (x : QuarticQuery.BitInput (Fin 2)) (b : Bool),
    QuarticQuery.SemanticReview.orTwo x = Option.some b → 2 / 3 < QuarticQuery.SemanticReview.orMixture.success x b

semantic_probes.question: Does replacing success at least two thirds with strictly greater success change a boundary case?

semantic_probes.authored_answer: One randomized query suffices for two-bit OR with the stated error bound. Zero queries cannot distinguish its two labels.
semantic_probes.question: How many randomized queries does two-bit OR require with success at least two thirds?

statement: For a (partial) Boolean function f, R(f) is the least q such that some probability distribution on deterministic decision trees of depth at most q satisfies Pr[T(x)=f(x)] >= 2/3 for every x in dom f. The query cap holds on every branch and every coin outcome.
